newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan signs EU accord at Malta conference.
newsitem.headline: Jordan signs EU accord at Malta conference.

text.p: Jordan initialed on Wednesday an association accord with the EU on the sidelines of a European-Mediterranean conference in Malta, Jordanian officials in Amman said.
They said the accord was reached after nearly two years of tough negotiations over a host of disputes, including intellectual property rights, agricultural quotas and political issues.
The partnership accord, to be implemented on January 1 1999, will help speed up negotiations for a pact with the World Trade Organisation (WTO) by year-end, the officials said.

Jordan receives over 30 percent of its imports from European Union countries while a fraction of its exports go to European markets. Fear of competition from European industry is balanced by hopes the accord will bring European multinationals investing in Jordan to create much needed jobs for the aid-dependant economy, officials say.

Jordan has now agreed under the terms of the accord to four lists of goods which if supplied by EU countries will have import duties either totally eliminated or abolished over a period from two to five years.

A list of 492 industrial goods originating in the EU will have import duties lifted immediately the accord comes into effect while another list of goods produced in Jordan will be given five years to adjust to EU competition.

A smaller non-exempt "negative" list includes cigarettes, alcholic beverages, small cars, used clothes, furniture and carpets. Officials say they secured this concession for both revenue purposes and to ensure protection for local industry.

The two sides finally reached a compromise over one of the thorniest issues surfacing in recent rounds which relates to the status of third country nationals and movement of illegal workers, mainly Palestinians and Iraqis, in Europe.

A declaration annexed to the accord will commit Jordan to adhering to international human rights conventions, replacing an earlier European insistence that Jordan takes responsiblity for any people entering the EU illegally from its territory.
